initial.summary: Two tutors and a QA tutor asked how to handle fictional phone numbers; the QA tutor reports that two versions of the note seem to differ. Current guidance identifies the older help-page wording as stale and gives the rule and its effective date.
initial.reasoning: The current FAQ and the dated clarification establish both the applicable rule and the specific help-page section that needs correction. The historical page explains the conflicting wording but cannot support current handling. Correcting that section is supported without further retrieval; no claim is made that the correction has already happened or that any reported task meets the fictional-placeholder conditions.

claims.text: Two tutors ask whether a fictional phone number requires quarantine or sensitive-information handling.
A QA tutor asks whether to quarantine a story containing a made-up phone number and reports that two open versions of the note seem to differ.

In the two tutor-started threads, the team lead instructs participants to hold a final general-rule update until the current rule and its change date are verified; in the earlier thread, the team lead also instructs participants to retain the surrounding fictional context with the flag.
Verified fictional placeholders alone do not require QN. Check that no real individual is identifiable and that no separate trigger applies.

The project-wide fictional-contact clarification took effect on September 10, 2026, at 13:00 UTC and replaced only the blanket initial-quarantine requirement for fictional contact details. Possible real-person identification, uncertain fictional context, or another required safety trigger still requires review under the applicable rules.

The older QN help page required initial quarantine even when contact details were claimed to be made up. Its Contact details section is superseded; the current FAQ says that older copy has not been rewritten and directs reporting it for correction.
The batch announcement directs retaining surrounding context and not extending the fictional-placeholder exception to unrelated controls.

- Retain the surrounding context with flagged tasks.
Replace only the blanket initial-quarantine requirement for fictional contact details; preserve unrelated safety and privacy controls.

### Q: Do fake phone numbers or emails in a story require QN?
Verified fictional placeholders alone do not. Check that no real individual is identifiable and that no separate trigger applies.

[Clarification SC-PII-2026-09-10](../decisions/safety_classification/safety_fictional_pii_clarification_2026-09-10.md) supersedes the blanket fictional-contact trigger in [QN help page v1.0](../instructions/history/safety_qn_help_page_v1.0.md). # SC-PII-2026-09-10 — Fictional contact details

**Decision owner:** Priya (U006), Team Lead  
**Issued and effective:** September 10, 2026, 09:00 America/New_York  
**Scope:** Safety Classification project; the fictional-contact branch of QN handling.

## Clarification
Clearly fictional placeholder phone numbers or email addresses alone do not require QN when the surrounding evidence establishes that no real individual is identifiable.

If contact details could identify a real person, the fictional context is uncertain, or another required safety trigger applies, retain the task for review under the applicable rules. This clarification does not waive those separate controls.

## Superseded wording
This replaces the blanket initial-quarantine requirement for fictional contact details in the **Contact details** section of [QN help page v1.0](../../instructions/history/safety_qn_help_page_v1.0.md). It does not invalidate unrelated controls in that page.
